title: Laboratory Preparation of Ethanoic Acid (Acetic Acid)

provenance.source: Reference video supplied by the channel owner (downloaded from Facebook, 1280x720).
provenance.method: 24 frames sampled evenly plus full-size stills; scene timing is accurate to about 1.5 s.
provenance.audio_finding: The file has no audio stream.
provenance.reuse: Use as a style and structure reference; rebuild with your own models, wording and brand.

builder_instructions: Recreate a 36 s landscape 3D walkthrough of a distillation rig in one continuous camera move. The camera visits the reaction flask, the colour change, the condenser and the receiver, then pulls back for the balanced equation. Solid blue label chips with leader lines name each part; a white caption bar at the bottom carries one numbered sentence per step.

intent.goal: Explain how ethanol is oxidised to ethanoic acid and collected by distillation.
intent.audience: Secondary school chemistry students (IGCSE, GCSE, A-level).
intent.takeaway: Acidified dichromate oxidises ethanol; the acid distils over through a water-cooled condenser.
intent.hook: The orange mixture turns green as it reacts.

materials.glass: glossy clear glass with strong white reflections
materials.mantle: glossy blue shell with a glowing orange well

style.background: seamless white-to-pale-blue studio; objects far from the camera blur slightly
style.motion_language: one smooth dolly through the rig; labels fade in with their leader lines; nothing overlaps the caption bar

title_chip.style: solid blue rounded box, white text

layout.labels: placed beside the part, joined by a thin blue line ending in a ringed dot

end_cards.equation: top centre, white card with blue border

moves.shot: wide: whole rig from the front left
close on the round-bottom flask and heating mantle
medium on the condenser, tracking right
close on the condenser outlet and the conical flask
pull back to the wide view

objects.contents: orange liquid that turns green, with bubbles

objects.note: blue body, glowing orange well, on a stirrer base with a dial
red column, through a cork in the flask neck
slopes down to the right; droplets move inside
one hose to the lower inlet, one long loop from the upper outlet

science.topic: oxidation of a primary alcohol; distillation

equations.verified_here: C 2, H 6, O 3 on each side

claims.text: Orange Cr₂O₇²⁻ is reduced to green Cr³⁺ as ethanol is oxidised
Cold water enters the condenser at the lower end and leaves at the upper end

notes: School courses usually specify heating under reflux for complete oxidation to the acid, then distillation; the video shows distillation only. Decide which your syllabus needs before reusing the storyline.

audio.note: Silent file; add your own music bed.

timeline.caption: Ethanol is oxidised to ethanoic acid
timeline.visual: Whole rig; title chip fades in.

timeline.caption: 1 · Gentle heating of ethanol with acidified K₂Cr₂O₇
timeline.visual: Push in to the flask; the well glows, the liquid bubbles.

timeline.caption: 2 · Orange Cr₂O₇²⁻ is reduced to green Cr³⁺ as ethanol is oxidised
timeline.visual: The liquid changes from orange through olive to green.

timeline.caption: 3 · Cold water enters the condenser at the lower end, leaves at the upper end
timeline.visual: Track along the condenser; small blue beads show the water moving.

timeline.caption: 4 · Vapour condenses and ethanoic acid drips into the conical flask

Wide view, the flask now green.

avoid: more than three labels on screen
captions longer than one line at 1080p
qa_checklist: Water enters the condenser at the lower end.
The colour runs orange to green, never the reverse.
Every label's line ends on the part it names.
